definitions.explanation: Language as used in writing, as opposed to spoken language. Encompasses the vocabulary, grammar, and style characteristic of written communication.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{言葉|ことば}と{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}は{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: Written language and spoken language are different.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}の{書|か}き{言葉|ことば}には{漢語|かんご}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Japanese written language contains many Sino-Japanese words.

examples.japanese: この{表現|ひょうげん}は{書|か}き{言葉|ことば}としては{固|かた}すぎるので、もう{少|すこ}し{柔|やわ}らかい{言|い}い{方|かた}にしましょう。
examples.english: This expression is too stiff as written language, so let's use a softer way of saying it.

notes:
A compound of {書|か}き (writing) and {言葉|ことば} (language; words). In Japanese, the gap between written and spoken language is significant. Written Japanese tends to use more Sino-Japanese compounds ({漢語|かんご}), longer sentences, and formal grammar, while spoken Japanese uses more native Japanese words ({和語|わご}), contractions, and casual forms.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書|か}き{言葉|ことば}と{話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}: written and spoken language
- {書|か}き{言葉|ことば}の{表現|ひょうげん}: written expression
- {書|か}き{言葉|ことば}で{書|か}く: to write in written-style language

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {話|はな}し{言葉|ことば}: spoken language — the counterpart to {書|か}き{言葉|ことば}
- {文語|ぶんご}: literary language — specifically the classical written style, as opposed to modern written Japanese
- {口語|こうご}: colloquial language — modern spoken style, often contrasted with {文語|ぶんご}
